# Saved OpenAPI spec excerpts

Each pair is a real breaking change between two releases of a provider's own spec, trimmed to the schemas and paths involved: every line is copied unchanged, the rest of the spec was left out. The tests replay one release to the next and check the events.

The Elasticsearch copies keep `openapi`, `info` and the paths involved, every line unchanged; the 9.2 copy's paths are all gone in 9.2, so its `"paths": {}` is the one line that isn't in the original.

The Algolia copies are trimmed by lines: `openapi`, `info` and the paths involved, every line copied unchanged; `components` left out.

The Supabase copies keep each value unchanged but are re-indented: the source is Prettier-formatted (objects on one line where they fit), and minified on one line before 2025.

The Sentry copies keep `openapi`, `info`, `servers` and the path items involved, whole, in their original order except that `servers` comes before `paths`, every line copied unchanged (bar the trailing comma after a path item that's now last); `components` and `tags` left out. Each pair gives the same events as the full files, with the filter and with the variants the tests use (flag only, "deprecat" anywhere). The tests serve them as GitHub would, with each commit's date and each tag's release date.

The Neon copies are excerpts, not whole files: the spec says its license is "Proprietary" whatever the license of the repo or package that ships it. The JSON copies keep `openapi`, `servers`, `info` (without its `contact`) and the path items involved, whole and in their original order, every line copied unchanged (bar the trailing comma after a member that's now last); `components` left out. The YAML copies keep, by lines, `openapi`, `servers`, `info`'s `title`, `version` and `license`, and the path items involved; they're a different source from the plugin's (the npm package @neondatabase/api-client, succeeded by @neon/sdk and not released since 2.7.3), used only to check that the removal of an operation marked deprecated is kept.
The Convex copies keep `openapi`, `info`, `servers` and the path items involved, whole and in their original order, every line copied unchanged (bar the trailing comma after a path item or schema that's now last); the usage-limit pair also keeps the component schemas those operations reach, the log stream pair none. The source is FSL-1.1-Apache-2.0 (each version becomes Apache-2.0 two years after it's published), which allows copying for a permitted purpose; these are short excerpts kept for testing, but a maintainer should confirm that before release. Each pair gives the same changes as the full files, with and without the filter. The management API spec (`management-openapi.json`, `info.license` `LicenseRef-Convex`, not defined anywhere in the repo) is neither read nor saved.
The PlanetScale copies are trimmed by lines: everything before `paths:` (`openapi`, `info`), then the path items involved, whole, and the two-line `servers` block (`https://api.planetscale.com/v1`, the same in every version), every line copied unchanged; the other paths, `tags`, `security`, `x-readme` and `components` left out. The file states no license, so only what the tests need is kept. The golden pair gives the full files' 5 deprecations (their only ones), the drop-test pair their 7 removals (their only ones). The tests serve them as GitHub would, with each commit's date.

The Appwrite copies keep `openapi`, `info`, `servers` and the path items involved, whole and in their original order; `tags`, `components` and `externalDocs` left out. They're re-serialized the way the originals are written (4-space indent, `/` written `\/`, non-ASCII as `\u` escapes), which gives every original line back byte for byte when nothing is left out, so every kept line is unchanged bar a trailing comma. The 1.9.x pair keeps the paths of the 14 operations deprecated in `7d74bf9f`, the 2.4.x pair the paths of the 13 operations that lost the server platform in `06e6fafa`, the 1.7.x and 1.8.x pair the paths of the 21 operations flagged only for an SDK method rename. With the full files the plugin gives the same results: 14 events, none, and none (50, from the rest of 1.8.x's Databases deprecations, with the 21 renames still left out).

Stripe's spec isn't saved here: its tests use small specs written inline.

The Flagsmith copies are trimmed by lines: `openapi`, `info` and `servers`, then the path items involved (`paths: {}` where none remain, the one line in `v2.287.0.yaml` that isn't in the original) and, under `components: schemas:`, every schema those paths' request bodies reach, transitively, whole and in original order, every line copied unchanged; `tags` and `security` left out. `FeatureValue`, `FeatureValueTypeEnum` and `MultivariateValue` are kept unchanged in both files because the real spec still has them at `v2.287.0` (other, unremoved operations use them too); every other schema the removed paths reached (`DeleteSegmentOverride`, `EnvironmentDefault`, `FeatureIdentifier`, `FeatureUpdateSegmentData`, `SegmentIdentifier`, `SegmentOverride`, `UpdateFlag`, `UpdateFlagV2`) really is gone in `v2.287.0`, confirmed against the full file. The drop-test pair is two commits, not tags, kept whole but for the same trim (`TokenExchangeResponse` and the `Master API Key` security scheme, the only two places that commit touched `openapi.yaml`).
